title: PTE Academic: How to Avoid Repeating Speaking Module Pitfalls
author: Pearson Certified Trainer
excerpt: Discover why computer algorithms dock pronunciation marks and learn how to position your microphone and maintain vocal flow for maximum score outcomes.
body:
Unlike traditional human-graded language exams, the Pearson Test of English (PTE) is scored entirely by computer algorithms. This computer-automated grading brings a unique set of parameters that candidates must master, particularly in the Speaking module where minor technical blunders can drop your overall fluency scores.

Here are the top speaking mistakes candidates make and how to avoid them during computer testing:

1. Mic Position is Crucial: Never place the microphone directly in front of your mouth. The sound of your breathing (plosive air bursts) will distort the audio, leading the algorithm to miss key words. Instead, position the microphone tip level with your nose or just below your lower lip.

2. Avoid Hesitations (The 3-Second Rule): If you remain silent for more than 3 seconds after the microphone opens, the recording will automatically close, and you will receive zero marks for that task. If you stumble, immediately continue speaking; do not repeat words or pause.

3. Fluidity Over Precision: The PTE algorithm measures Oral Fluency based on a smooth, constant speech flow. If you speak too slowly or correct your pronunciation mid-sentence, the system will dock points. Focus on maintaining a steady rhythm and natural phrasing.

4. The Intonation Trap: Avoid speaking in a flat, robotic tone. The algorithm checks for word stress and natural intonation. Ensure you raise and lower your pitch appropriately, emphasizing content words (nouns and verbs) over grammar particles.
